MAR 1 0 2025 MS. DINA C. PASCUAL Municipal Indigenous People Mandatory Representative Municipality od Dr. Jose P. Rizal Province of Palawan Dear Ms. Pascual: We refer to your earlier letter dated 16 August 2024 requesting for the Department's opinion on the following issues: I. 2. Are there any specific guidelines issued by the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) that govem the selection of IPMRs in Local Government Units (LGUs), in addition to those prescribed by the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP)? Is it legally permissible to proceed with the implementation of projects with Ancestral Domains without securing the Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC) of the Indigenous Cultural Communities/lndigenous Peoples (ICCs/lPs) provided that the project proponent has obtained a resolution or endorsement from the concemed Local Govemment Unit (LGU)? For your first query, as far as this Department is concemed, we have issued Memorandum Circular No. 2010-119 dated 20 October 2010 and entitled "Mandatory Representation of Indigenous Cultural Communities or Indigenous Peoples in Policy Making Bodies and Other Local Legislative Councils". The said Department issuance supplements the provisions of NCIP Administrative Order No. 001, s. 20091 However, considering that NCIP has subsequently issued Administrative Order No. 3, s. 20182 and CEB Resolution No. 08-008-2020, s. 20203, we suggest that you refer to these issuances for an updated guidance. With regard to the second query, the indigenous people's free, prior, and informed 1 National Guidelines for the Mandatory Representaiton of Indigenous Peoples in Local Legislative 2 Revised Nafional Guidelines for the Mandatory Representation of Indigenous Peoples in Local Legislative Councils and Policy-making Bodies 3 A RESOLUTION AMENDING SECTIONS 9 (F), 12,13 and 18 (d) OF NATIONAL COMMISSION ON INDIGENOUS PEOPLES ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER NO. 3, SERIES OF 2018, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "REVISED GUIDELINES FOK THE MANDATORY REPRESENTARION OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES IN LOCAL LEGISLATIVE MAKING BODIES," AND AMENDING ALL REFERENCES THERETO FROM "ASPIRANTS" TO "NOMINEES" AND THEREBY MAKING ADDENDUM TO CEB RESOLUTION NO. 08-006-2020 Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

consent (FPIC) is mandatory under Republic Act No. 8371, otherwise known as the Indigenous People's Rights Act (IPRA). As prescribed under Section 59 of the IPRA, any project involving the extraction, development and utilization of natural resources within the ancestral domain should be carried out after obtaining the consent of indigenous peoples within the impact area, to wit: — All departments and SECTION 59. Certification Precondition. other govemmental agencies shall henceforth be strictly enjoined from issuing, renewing, or granting any concession, license or lease, or entering into any production-sharing agreement, without prior certification from the NCIP that the area affected does not overlap with any ancestral domain. Such certification shall only be issued after a field based investigation is conducted by the Ancestral Domains Office of the area concemed: Provided, That no certification shall be issued by the NCIP without the free and prior informed and written consent of ICCs/IPs concemed: Provided, further, That no department, govemment agency or govemment-owned or -controlled corporation may issue new concession, license, lease, or production sharing agreement while there is a pending application for a CADT: Provided, finally, That the ICCs/IPs shall have the right to stop or suspend, in accordance with this Act, any project that has not satisfied the requirement of this consultation process. (Emphasis and underscoring supplied) In addition, NCIP promulgated Administrative Order No. 3., s. 2012. This set of guidelines stipulates that all activities involving the utilization, extraction or development of natural resources are subject to the Indigenous Cultural Communities/lndigenous Peoples' free and prior informed consent Sec. 7, par (5), of NCIP AP No. 2, s. 2012, provides: Section 7. Powers, Duties and Functions of the Indigenous Political Structures. The ICCs4Ps through the elders/leaders of the IPS shall have these powers, duties and functions as enumerated in the IPRA, but not limited to the following: (5) To uphold the Free and Prior Informed Consent (FPIC) process relative to all activities involving the utilization, extraction or development of natural resources; As demonstrated in the phraseology of Section 59 of the IPRA and in Administrative Order NO. 3., s. 2012 as quoted above, FPIC is an indispensable and integral precondition on all activities that affect the exploration, development and use of natural resources within an ancestral domain. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. Page 2 of 2
